topic: Sharp lag-refinement bounds for micro controlled direct effects: for finite binary processes with directed effects restricted to positive lags 1,…,L, a bounded observed window, and a directed/bidirected summary causal graph, fix one common controlled direct-effect query over the positive-lag possible-parent set and define its envelope over all compatible full-time ADMG refinements and semi-Markovian SCMs reproducing an algebraically encoded positive observed law; compile the fiber into canonical response-function polynomial programs and prove terminating exact real-algebraic certification with derived bit complexity, endpoint attainment and SCM reconstruction, collapse to Ferreira–Assaad adjustment under their conditions, strict tightening over graph-free order-only bounds on a graphically characterized relative-open family, and simultaneous-multinomial whole-set inference with tie-aware EasyRCA comparisons. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For N=|V|(H+1), bounded positive lags give finitely many full-time refinements; fixed-graph canonical response tables turn each refinement into a compact polynomial program, and real-algebraic quantifier elimination isolates attained endpoints and reconstructs algebraic-weight SCMs. In the binary temporal-IV witness, matching primal/dual calculations give graph-aware endpoints 0.285 and 0.685 versus order-only endpoints -0.1975 and 0.8025; every response-coupling cell is at least 0.005, so continuity plausibly extends strict tightening to a relative-open family. A rational box-simplex multinomial confidence polytope supplies simultaneous finite-sample coverage, with joint pairwise endpoint optimization reporting ties when effect differences include zero. Checks covered H=L, γ=L, cyclic summaries with acyclic positive-lag unrollings, bow graphs, non-clique bidirected districts, simplex boundaries, zero-cell confidence regions, and the closest fixed-graph, order-only, and summary-graph papers; no collision or counterexample was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that merging observationally and query-equivalent response signatures preserves exactly the attainable (P,q) image and semi-Markovian factorization with overlapping independent latent parents, and derive the quotient-size bound. EARLY KILL TEST: On binary A↔B↔C with independent edge latents and one lagged arrow into C, exhaust raw and quotiented canonical signatures and compare their projected (P,q) semialgebraic sets by exact elimination; any separating witness forces an unquotiented pivot and kills the quotient-complexity claim.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether observationally and query-equivalent response signatures can be merged without changing the attainable joint image of the observed law and micro CDE when semi-Markovian factorization uses independent, overlapping edge latents, and derive the quotient size or a minimal separating counterexample.

source_refs.claim: Proves signature-state partitioning preserves an order-only LP by redistributing each quotient-cell mass over raw signatures; the lift does not impose overlapping independent edge-latent factorization.
source_refs.author: Eric Rossetto and Alessandro Antonucci

source_refs.claim: Introduces mDAGs because ordinary mixed graphs do not encode all marginal models generated by latent-variable DAGs.
source_refs.author: Robin J. Evans

source_refs.excerpt: the row face can strictly outer-relax the true sparse/cross-district compatibility projection
A correct compiler must use one copy of every Z_{t,x} within each fixed-sign endpoint circuit
simultaneous realization when virtual-edge paths share or branch through ancestors of S

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rossetto–Antonucci's quotient lift is valid for an unrestricted distribution over raw response signatures, whereas independent edge latents constrain raw masses to a multilinear product-image, especially on overlapping districts such as A↔B↔C. Evans's latent-margin results show that equality of displayed ADMG constraints need not preserve the hidden-DAG marginal model. The prior Layer-3 run observed that a row-face quotient can outer-relax cross-district compatibility, and the shared-coupling run showed that duplicating one response variable across branches changes the optimizer. Thus the first unresolved step is a factorization-preserving raw-to-quotient lift, not merely equality of observational and query columns.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient quotient-preservation theorem with an explicit product-factorization-preserving lift and quotient-cardinality bound, or an exact semialgebraic separating witness on binary A↔B↔C with one lagged arrow.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing explains why reductions of hidden-variable models must preserve the full attainable distribution class, not only visible mixed-graph constraints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden-variable margins obey non-obvious constraints -> model reductions must preserve the attainable distribution class -> signature merging may erase latent independence -> characterize exactly when the quotient preserves the joint observed-law/query image

method_exemplars.technique: Partition signatures by equality of all observational constraints and query values, push mass to quotient cells, and lift it back to establish equality of feasible images.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact quotient argument to adapt; its unrestricted lift must be replaced by one compatible with independent overlapping edge latents.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize finite functional causal structures polynomially and eliminate latent parameters to compare observable semialgebraic images.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact image comparison supplies the decisive small-instance test for whether the raw and quotient projected (P,q) sets coincide.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile discrete response functions, observed-cell constraints, and causal queries into polynomial programs, then propagate an observed-law confidence region through endpoint optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the quotient is sound, the same image-preserving compiler must also preserve every confidence-fiber endpoint used by the estimation rung.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite binary positive-lag process and directed/bidirected summary graph, determine the sharp envelope of one common micro controlled direct effect over all compatible full-time ADMG refinements and semi-Markovian SCMs, including the exact collapse frontier for the Ferreira–Assaad adjustment functional.

source_refs.claim: Gives sufficient graphical conditions for identifying average controlled micro direct effects with hidden confounding, but does not give sharp sets outside that regime.
source_refs.author: Simon Ferreira and Charles K. Assaad

source_refs.claim: Reduces discrete causal bounding problems for a specified causal model to response-function polynomial programs and computes sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Reduces point-identification decisions in a known bounded-lag infinite time-series ADMG to a finite segment, but does not optimize over unknown summary-graph refinements.
source_refs.author: Erik L. Jahn, Karthik Karnik, and Leonard J. Schulman
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275

source_refs.excerpt: position H_star as a precise nonidentification boundary beyond Ferreira--Assaad Assumption 1
two exact acyclic refinements share the entire strictly positive observed law yet their macro effects differ

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ferreira–Assaad identifies the query under a restricted summary-graph regime, while Autobounds assumes one declared discrete causal model rather than a union of lag refinements. Jahn–Karnik–Schulman supplies a finite-window reduction for a known time-series ADMG, not agreement across unknown refinements. The prior arbitrary-cluster run further shows that point identification within each refinement does not ensure a common functional over their union: two refinements can reproduce one positive law and disagree. The missing theorem must therefore equate the refinement-indexed polynomial union with the summary-graph fiber and establish either common adjustment or a same-law countermodel pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set theorem expressing the envelope as extrema of finitely many canonical polynomial programs, with endpoint-attaining SCMs and a graphical collapse theorem returning the Ferreira–Assaad functional or constructing same-positive-law unequal-CDE refinements outside the collapse class.

writing_exemplar.why: It moves directly from temporally abstracted graphs to micro direct-effect queries and cleanly separates graphical identification from the unresolved region.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full-time causal graphs are unavailable -> summary graphs omit lags and may be cyclic or confounded -> micro controlled direct effects are identified under published graphical conditions -> characterize the sharp set and collapse frontier beyond those conditions

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize structural functions into response types, translate compatibility and the query into polynomial constraints and objectives, and prove sharpness by reconstructing SCMs from feasible response weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every fixed full-time refinement is a discrete latent-variable bounding problem; the new argument adds a finite union without losing attainability.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bounded direct and latent lags to reduce an infinite time-series identification question to a finite graph segment while tracking temporal districts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A rigorous finite-window reduction is required before response-function optimization can cover every admissible full-time model.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile fixing-derived hidden-variable graphical functionals into influence-function estimators and characterize their asymptotic laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On the collapse class the returned adjustment expression is an observed-law functional with a concrete estimator and limit-law rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a terminating exact algorithm for rationally encoded positive observed laws that certifies every endpoint of the finite lag-refinement micro-CDE envelope, reconstructs an endpoint-attaining algebraic-weight semi-Markovian SCM, and gives bit and certificate-size complexity in the causal input parameters.

source_refs.claim: Provides numerical spatial branch-and-bound with valid outer bounds and epsilon-sharpness, not symbolic endpoint isolation, exact termination, or causal-model-specific bit complexity.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Gives explicit combinatorial and algebraic complexity bounds for quantifier elimination over real closed fields.
source_refs.author: Saugata Basu, Richard Pollack, and Marie-Françoise Roy

source_refs.excerpt: State an explicit input encoding and worst-case complexity/output-size bound for CAD_m and CAD_conf
paired-SCM extraction requires a new sample-point, representation, decoding, and correctness architecture

open_problems.why_unsolved: Autobounds yields arbitrarily small numerical gaps but not exact algebraic endpoints or termination certificates. Generic real quantifier elimination gives decidability and worst-case bounds, yet this input is a disjunction of compact refinement-specific polynomial images with simplex and independent-latent factorization constraints. The finite-plate reviewer explicitly identified input encoding, bit complexity, and output size as missing, while the Layer-3 run found that an exact range formula does not itself decode an SCM. The first missing step is a size-controlled first-order-real encoding whose algebraic sample points can be converted back into graph-compatible response tables and latent distributions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact real-algebraic endpoint-isolation and witness-extraction algorithm with a proved bit-operation and output-size bound, returning isolating polynomials and intervals for each endpoint plus a checkable algebraic-weight SCM that attains it.

writing_exemplar.why: Its arc from bespoke causal bounds to a general response-function compiler is the natural framing for replacing epsilon-sharp output by exact certificates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete causal bounds are algebraically bespoke -> response functions compile them into polynomial programs -> numerical optimization gives reusable epsilon-sharp answers -> finite refinement fibers require exact endpoint certificates, complexity bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses

method_exemplars.technique: Express hidden-variable compatibility and causal bounds as first-order formulas over the reals and eliminate latent parameters to obtain exact observable and query constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate is the same projection problem, augmented by a finite temporal-refinement disjunction and endpoint witness extraction.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply block-structured real quantifier elimination with separate control of polynomial count, degree, coefficient bits, and quantified-variable blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those parameters can be instantiated from response-table and refinement counts to derive the required bit bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize causal endpoints over confidence-region constraints on observed discrete probabilities and transfer the input region's coverage to the causal outer bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact compiler should accept a rational confidence polytope and return certified finite-sample confidence endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the directed/bidirected summary-graph or exposed-face conditions under which the graph-aware lag-refinement micro-CDE envelope is strictly narrower than graph-free order-only bounds on a nonempty relative-open family of positive observed laws.

source_refs.claim: Derives tight LP bounds for arbitrary counterfactual queries using only the partial causal order and constructs attaining SCMs.
source_refs.author: Eric Rossetto and Alessandro Antonucci

source_refs.claim: Uses invariant PAG information to derive causal-effect bounds tighter than graph-free natural bounds, showing that partial graphical structure can sharpen identified sets.
source_refs.author: Alexis Bellot

source_refs.excerpt: a checkable contact-set or exposed-face condition for exactly when the optimized interval is strictly narrower
Its lower and upper excess widths over the shared interval both equal (1-epsilon)/2 > 0

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rossetto–Antonucci proves tightness for the order-only comparator, and Bellot shows that invariant partial-graph information can tighten bounds, but neither gives a temporal summary-graph criterion separating robust structural tightening from a pointwise numerical accident. The finite-plate reviewer identified the missing contact-set or exposed-face bridge, while the shared-coupling proposal demonstrates that an exact common-variable restriction can yield a persistent two-sided gap. The unresolved proof step is a dual separator that excludes an order-only extremizer and remains strict under relative perturbations of the observed law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graphical or exposed-face sufficient-condition theorem with an exact rational primal-dual witness, positive endpoint-separation margins, and a quantified relative-open neighborhood on which graph-aware bounds remain strictly tighter.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the central comparison as the value of retaining invariant graphical information when the complete causal diagram is unavailable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A unique causal graph is often unjustified -> weaker graph summaries retain invariant restrictions -> those restrictions can tighten graph-free bounds -> determine when a temporal summary graph yields robust strict tightening for a micro CDE

method_exemplars.technique: Represent query-implied causal orders by a canonical response-signature LP and prove tightness through explicit SCM reconstruction from feasible optima.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its attaining order-only SCM is the exact comparator that a graph-aware strictness certificate must exclude.

method_exemplars.technique: Use generalized-moment duality and supporting hyperplanes to characterize endpoint contact sets and separation between nested moment classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired robust strictness criterion is an exposed-face statement for two nested attainable (P,q) sets.

method_exemplars.technique: Re-optimize target projections over a calibrated confidence-feasible moment set and establish coverage under changing active constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An inference rung must distinguish population tightening from sampling variation near exposed-face switches.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop simultaneous finite-sample inference for the vector of lag-refinement micro-CDE lower and upper endpoints and all pairwise endpoint contrasts from one multinomial observed-window sample, with a tie declared exactly when zero remains feasible for the corresponding contrast.

source_refs.claim: EasyRCA compares direct effects for root-cause localization under an acyclic, causally sufficient summary graph, but does not use partially identified envelopes with simultaneous tie-aware inference.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad, Imad Ez-Zejjari, and Lei Zan

source_refs.claim: Constructs finite-sample confidence regions for the complete multinomial parameter with uniform coverage over the probability simplex.
source_refs.author: Matthew L. Malloy, Ardhendu Tripathy, and Robert D. Nowak

source_refs.excerpt: One explicitly calibrated transition-data event covers the whole vector of identified mean-credit intervals
Wald inference is restricted to a C1 branch extension with locally stable ambient-simplex covariance rank

open_problems.why_unsolved: A joint multinomial confidence region can be propagated through optimization, but the endpoint map here is a nonsmooth min/max over latent response weights and a discrete refinement union; active refinements and optimizers can switch or tie. EasyRCA's point-effect tests and scalar partially identified intervals do not provide joint coverage for all endpoints and contrasts. Prior work supplies a one-event simultaneous-fiber template, while the arbitrary-cluster review records that branchwise Wald inference fails at guard and rank switches. The missing argument is a single set-containment event whose image under joint endpoint and contrast optimization remains valid at boundaries and zero cells.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample simultaneous-coverage theorem and exact optimization procedure returning intervals for every envelope endpoint and pairwise contrast, with a sound zero-feasibility tie rule and consistency away from ties.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the downstream decision problem—root-cause comparison by direct effects—and motivates uncertainty-aware ties instead of forced rankings.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Collective anomalies need actionable root-cause localization -> summary graphs reduce the candidate set -> candidates are compared through direct effects -> replace point comparisons by simultaneous set-valued comparisons with explicit ties under graph and lag uncertainty

method_exemplars.technique: Invert multinomial sampling probabilities to construct a confidence subset of the probability simplex and prove uniform finite-sample coverage by a covering-collection argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: One covered observed-law vector can drive every endpoint and contrast optimization simultaneously without separate marginal events.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed an observed-cell confidence region into response-function optimization and transfer input-region coverage to causal outer-bound coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required proof repeats this feasible-set-inclusion argument for a union of refinements and a vector of endpoint and contrast objectives.

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional differentiability and derivative-aware resampling for minima, maxima, and other kinked functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Optimizer and refinement switches create the directional, non-Wald behavior relevant near ties.

literature_map:
Ferreira and Assaad (UAI 2026, arXiv:2410.23975) identify average controlled and natural micro direct effects from summary causal graphs under sufficient graphical conditions.
Ferreira and Assaad (AAAI 2024, arXiv:2306.16958) give complete graphical identification for linear direct effects without hidden confounding and finite adjustment sets.
Assaad et al. (UAI 2024, PMLR 244) reduce total-effect identification from summary and extended-summary time-series graphs to graphical conditions and adjustment.
Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (CLeaR 2025, arXiv:2504.20172) prove a bounded-segment reduction for ID in infinite time-series ADMGs with known bounded lags.
Duarte et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2109.13471) compile discrete causal bounding problems into response-function polynomial programs with sharp or epsilon-sharp output.
Rossetto and Antonucci (2026, arXiv:2608.24427) derive tight order-only counterfactual bounds and use response-signature quotienting with explicit SCM reconstruction.
Bellot (UAI 2024, arXiv:2311.07259) shows that invariant partial-graph information can sharpen graph-free causal bounds.
Evans (Scandinavian Journal of Statistics 2016, arXiv:1408.1809) uses mDAGs to retain hidden-variable structure that pairwise mixed graphs can erase.
Evans (UAI 2021, arXiv:2106.07523) identifies non-obvious dependence restrictions and qualified reductions in hidden-variable DAG margins.
Geiger and Meek (UAI 1999, arXiv:1301.6698) use real quantifier elimination for exact hidden-graph compatibility, identification, and bound questions.
Basu, Pollack, and Roy (JACM 1996, DOI 10.1145/235809.235813) provide explicit real-quantifier-elimination complexity controls.
Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, arXiv:2002.01044) construct uniformly covered finite-sample multinomial confidence regions.
Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (AISTATS 2023, arXiv:2303.04038) compare direct effects for EasyRCA but do not handle partial-ID envelopes or tie-aware simultaneous inference.
The live intersection is sharp partial identification over temporal refinements, factorization-safe quotienting, exact algebraic certification, robust strict tightening over order-only bounds, and whole-vector inference.
